title.zh: 卷一百十六 周書7: 世宗本紀三
title.en: Volume 116 Book of Later Zhou 18: Shizong Annals 3
title.raw: 卷一百十六 周書7: 世宗本紀三 Volume 116 Book of Later Zhou 18: Shizong Annals 3

sentences.zh: 顯德三年春正月乙未朔，帝不受朝賀。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the third year of Xiande, on the first day of the month, day yimao, the Emperor did not accept court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the first month of spring in the third year of Xiande, the emperor declined the usual New Year court congratulations.

sentences.zh: 前司空蘇禹珪卒。

translations.literal: The former Minister of Works Su Yugui died.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yugui, former Minister of Works, died.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，李穀奏，破淮賊於上窯。

translations.literal: On day dingyou, Li Gu memorialized that the Huainan rebels had been defeated at Shangyao.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Li Gu reported a victory over the Huainan rebels at Shangyao.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，發丁夫十萬城京師羅城。

translations.literal: On day wuxu, one hundred thousand corvée laborers were mobilized to fortify the outer wall of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, the court drafted one hundred thousand laborers to build up the capital's outer ramparts.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔取此月八日幸淮南。

translations.literal: On day gengzi, an edict set the eighth day of this month for the imperial visit to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, an edict scheduled the emperor's departure for Huainan on the eighth of the month.

sentences.zh: 殿中監馬從赟免所居官，坐幹沒外孫女霍氏之資產，為人所訟故也。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace Secretariat Ma Congyun was removed from his post for embezzling the property of his granddaughter née Huo, because he had been sued by others.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Congyun, Director of the Palace Secretariat, was dismissed from office for having embezzled his granddaughter Huo's estate after others brought suit against him.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以宣徽南院使向訓為權東京留守，以端明殿學士王樸為副留守。

translations.literal: On day xinchou, the Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat Xiang Xun was made acting military governor of the Eastern Capital, and the Academician of the Duanming Hall Wang Pu was made deputy military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Xiang Xun, commissioner of the southern bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was appointed acting military governor of the Eastern Capital, with Wang Pu of the Duanming Hall as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，車駕發京師，丁未，李穀奏，自壽州引軍退守正陽。

translations.literal: On day renyin the imperial carriage departed the capital; on day dingwei Li Gu memorialized that he had withdrawn his army from Shouzhou to hold Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the emperor left the capital; on dingwei Li Gu reported that he had pulled his forces back from Shouzhou to defend Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，李重進奏，大破淮賊於正陽，斬首二萬餘級，伏屍三十里，臨陣斬賊大將劉彥貞，生擒偏將鹹師朗已下，獲戎甲三十萬副、馬五百匹。

translations.literal: On day xinhai Li Chongjin memorialized that he had routed the Huainan rebels at Zhengyang, beheading more than twenty thousand; corpses lay for thirty li; in battle he slew the rebel general Liu Yanzhen and captured alive the deputy commanders Xian Shilang and others; he obtained three hundred thousand suits of armor and five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Li Chongjin reported a great victory at Zhengyang: over twenty thousand heads taken, the dead strewn for thirty li along the field. Liu Yanzhen, the rebels' chief general, was killed in the fighting; deputy commanders including Xian Shilang were captured alive; and the army seized three hundred thousand suits of armor and five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 先是，李穀駐軍於壽春城下，以攻其城，既而淮南援軍大至，乃與將佐謀曰：「賊軍舟棹將及正陽，我師無水戰之備，萬一橋梁不守，則大軍隔絕矣，不如全師退守正陽浮橋，以俟鑾輅。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Gu had encamped below Shouchun to attack the city; then Huainan reinforcements arrived in great numbers, and he consulted his officers, saying: "The rebel fleet will soon reach Zhengyang. Our army is not prepared for river fighting. If the bridge should not be held, the main force would be cut off. It is better to withdraw the whole army to guard the pontoon bridge at Zhengyang and await the imperial carriage."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Gu had camped beneath Shouchun to press the siege, but when large Huainan relief forces arrived he took counsel with his officers: "The enemy's boats will soon be upon Zhengyang. We have no means to fight on the water. If the bridge were lost, the main army would be stranded. Better to pull back in full strength to the pontoon bridge at Zhengyang and wait for the emperor."

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆以為然，遂燔其糧草而退。

translations.literal: " All the generals agreed, and they burned their grain and fodder and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all agreed, so they burned their stores and retreated.

sentences.zh: 軍回之際無復嚴整，公私之間頗多亡失，淮北役夫亦有陷於賊境者。

translations.literal: On the march back discipline was no longer strict; both public and private property suffered many losses, and corvée laborers north of the Huai also fell into enemy territory.
translations.idiomatic: The withdrawal was disorderly; government and private goods alike were widely lost, and laborers from north of the Huai were also caught behind enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，急詔侍衛都指揮使李重進率師赴之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of this, he urgently ordered the Commander of the Imperial Guards Li Chongjin to lead troops to the scene.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, the emperor urgently ordered Li Chongjin, commander of the imperial guards, to march to their aid.

sentences.zh: 時淮賊乘李穀退軍之勢，發戰棹數百艘沿淮而上，且張斷橋之勢，彥貞以大軍列陣而進。

translations.literal: At that time the Huainan rebels, taking advantage of Li Gu's withdrawal, sent several hundred warships up the Huai and also deployed to sever the bridge; Yanzhen advanced with a large army in battle order.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan rebels, emboldened by Li Gu's retreat, sent hundreds of warships upriver while posting forces to cut the bridge; Liu Yanzhen advanced in full battle array.

sentences.zh: 李重進既至正陽，聞淮軍在近，率諸將渡橋而進，與賊軍遇，重進等合勢擊之，一鼓而敗之。

translations.literal: When Li Chongjin reached Zhengyang and heard the Huainan army was near, he led his generals across the bridge to advance; they met the rebels, and Chongjin and the others combined their strength and attacked; at the first drum they routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin reached Zhengyang, learned the enemy was close, and led his officers across the bridge to engage. They met the rebel host, struck with combined force, and broke them at the first onset.

sentences.zh: （馬令《南唐書》：世宗親征，行至圉鎮，聞蒨軍卻，意唐兵必追之，遣李重進急趨正陽，曰：「唐兵且至，宜急擊之。

translations.literal: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang: When Shizong campaigned in person and reached Yuzhen, he heard that Gu's army had withdrawn and thought the Tang troops would surely pursue; he sent Li Chongjin in haste to Zhengyang, saying: "The Tang army is about to arrive—you should strike at once."
translations.idiomatic: (From Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang: On his personal campaign Shizong reached Yuzhen. Hearing that Li Gu had pulled back, he expected the Zhou forces to pursue and sent Li Chongjin hurrying to Zhengyang with the words, "The enemy is coming—strike quickly."

sentences.zh: 」彥貞等聞蒨退軍，皆以為怯，裨將鹹師朗曰：「追之可大獲。

translations.literal: " When Yanzhen and the others heard that Gu had withdrawn, they all thought him timid; the deputy commander Xian Shilang said: "If we pursue, we can win a great prize."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen and his officers, hearing of the withdrawal, took it for cowardice. Deputy commander Xian Shilang said, "A pursuit would bring rich spoils."

sentences.zh: 」劉仁贍使人喻之曰：「君來赴援，未交戰而敵人退，不可測也，慎勿追逐。

translations.literal: " Liu Renshan sent someone to admonish him: "You came to relieve the siege. The enemy withdrew before any battle was joined—their intent cannot be gauged. Take care not to pursue."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Renshan sent a messenger urging caution: "You came as reinforcements. They retreated before fighting—their move may be a trap. Do not chase."

sentences.zh: 君為大將，安危以之，脫有不利，大事去矣。

translations.literal: You are the chief commander; the army's safety rests on you. If anything goes wrong, the great cause is lost.
translations.idiomatic: As supreme commander you hold the army's fate. One misstep and the whole campaign is lost.

sentences.zh: 」前軍張全約亦曰：「不可追。

translations.literal: " The vanguard commander Zhang Quanyue also said: "Do not pursue."
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard officer Zhang Quanyue likewise warned, "Do not pursue."

sentences.zh: 」彥貞曰：「軍容在我，汝輩何知？

translations.literal: " Yanzhen said: "The conduct of the army is mine to decide—what do you people know?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen retorted, "The army answers to me—what do you know?"

sentences.zh: 沮吾事者斬！

translations.literal: Whoever obstructs my plan shall be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who blocks me will be executed!

sentences.zh: 」比至正陽，而重進先至，未及食而戰。

translations.literal: " By the time they reached Zhengyang, Chongjin had already arrived; battle began before they had eaten.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Zhengyang, Chongjin was already there; the fight began before Yanzhen's men had eaten.

sentences.zh: 彥貞施利刃於拒馬，又刻木為獸，號捷馬牌，以皮囊布鐵蒺藜於地。

translations.literal: Yanzhen set sharp blades on the abatis, also carved wooden beasts called "Swift Horse Boards," and spread iron caltrops on the ground from leather pouches.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen fixed blades to his abatis, set up carved wooden beasts called "Swift Horse Boards," and strewed iron caltrops from leather bags across the ground.

sentences.zh: 周兵見而知其怯，一鼓而敗之，彥貞死於陣。）〉

translations.literal: The Zhou troops saw this and knew his timidity; at one drum they defeated him, and Yanzhen died on the field.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou soldiers saw through his show of force; one charge routed him, and Yanzhen fell in battle.)〉

sentences.zh: 殺獲之外，降者三千餘人，皆為我將趙晁所殺。

translations.literal: Apart from those killed and captured, more than three thousand who surrendered were all put to death by our general Zhao Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the slain and captured, over three thousand who had surrendered were also killed by our general Zhao Chao.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，車駕至正陽。

translations.literal: On day jiayin the imperial carriage reached Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the emperor arrived at Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 以侍衛都指揮使李重進為淮南道行營都招討使，命宰臣李穀判壽州行府事。

translations.literal: The Commander of the Imperial Guards Li Chongjin was made overall commander of the Huainan campaign headquarters, and the chief minister Li Gu was ordered to oversee the Shouzhou field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin, commander of the imperial guards, was appointed supreme commander of the Huainan campaign, and Chief Minister Li Gu was assigned to run the Shouzhou field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，車駕渡淮。

translations.literal: On day yimao the imperial carriage crossed the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the emperor crossed the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，至壽州城下，營於州西北淝水之陽，詔移正陽浮橋於下蔡。

translations.literal: On day bingchen he reached below the walls of Shouzhou and encamped on the south bank of the Fei northwest of the prefecture; an edict ordered the pontoon bridge at Zhengyang moved to Xiaocai.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen he came beneath Shouzhou and pitched camp south of the Fei River northwest of the city; the pontoon bridge at Zhengyang was ordered relocated to Xiaocai.

sentences.zh: 庚申，耀兵於城下。

translations.literal: On day gengshen he displayed his troops below the city.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen he paraded his army before the walls.

sentences.zh: （《春明退朝錄》云：家有《範魯公雜錄》，記世宗親征忠正，駐蹕城下，中夜有白虹自淝水起，亙數丈，下貫城中，數刻方沒。）〉

translations.literal: (Retiring from Court at Chunming records: The family possesses Fan Lugong's Miscellaneous Records, which notes that when Shizong campaigned in person against Zhongzheng and halted below the city, at midnight a white rainbow rose from the Fei, spanning several zhang and piercing down into the city; only after some moments did it vanish.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Retiring from Court at Chunming notes that the author's family kept Fan Zhongyan's Miscellaneous Records, which describes Shizong's personal campaign against Zhongzheng: while he encamped below the walls, a white rainbow rose from the Fei at midnight, arched several zhang across the sky, and plunged into the city before fading some time later.)〉

sentences.zh: 壬戌，今上奏，破淮賊萬餘眾於渦口，斬偽兵馬都監何延錫等，獲戰船五十艘。

translations.literal: On day renxu the heir apparent memorialized that more than ten thousand Huainan rebels had been defeated at Wokou; the false Director of Horse and Infantry He Yanxi and others were beheaded, and fifty warships were captured.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the heir apparent reported routing over ten thousand rebels at Wokou, executing the enemy's Director of Horse and Infantry He Yanxi and others, and seizing fifty warships.

sentences.zh: 二月丙寅，幸下蔡。

translations.literal: In the second month, on day bingyin, he visited Xiaocai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingyin, the emperor went to Xiaocai.

sentences.zh: 斬前濟州馬軍都指揮使康儼於路左，坐橋道不謹也。

translations.literal: The former Commander of the Cavalry of Jizhou Kang Yi was beheaded by the roadside for negligence regarding bridges and roads.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yi, former commander of the Jizhou horse army, was beheaded along the route for failing to maintain bridges and roads properly.

sentences.zh: 朗州節度使王進逵奏，領兵入淮南界。

translations.literal: The military governor of Langzhou Wang Jinkui memorialized that he had led troops into Huainan territory.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinkui, military governor of Langzhou, reported leading his army into Huainan.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，廬壽巡檢使司超奏，破淮賊三千於盛唐，獲都監偽吉州刺史高弼以獻。

translations.literal: On day wuchen the Inspector of Lu and Shou Si Chao memorialized that three thousand Huainan rebels had been defeated at Shengtang; the false Director and false prefect of Jizhou Gao Bi was captured and presented.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Si Chao, inspector of Lu and Shou, reported defeating three thousand rebels at Shengtang and presenting the captured enemy director and false prefect of Jizhou, Gao Bi.

sentences.zh: 詔釋之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his release.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him released.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書張昭奏，準詔撰集兵法，分為十卷，凡四十二門，目之為《制旨兵法》，上之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Zhang Zhao memorialized that by imperial order he had compiled military methods in ten juan with forty-two sections in all, entitled Imperially Directed Military Methods, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao, Minister of War, presented the ten-scroll Imperially Directed Military Methods he had compiled by edict, comprising forty-two sections in all.

sentences.zh: 優詔褒美，仍以器幣賜之。

translations.literal: A gracious edict praised him, and he was also given vessels and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a commendatory edict and rewarded him with ritual vessels and silks.

sentences.zh: 壬申，今上奏，破淮賊萬五千人於清流山，乘勝攻下滁州，擒偽命江州節度使、充行營應援使皇甫暉，常州團練使、充應援都監姚鳳以獻。

translations.literal: On day renshen the heir apparent memorialized that fifteen thousand Huainan rebels had been defeated at Qingliushan; pressing the victory he took Chuzhou and captured the false appointee military governor of Jiangzhou and campaign relief commissioner Huangfu Hui, and the false regiment commander of Changzhou and relief director Yao Feng, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the heir apparent reported defeating fifteen thousand rebels at Qingliushan, then storming Chuzhou and capturing the enemy's Jiangzhou governor and relief commissioner Huangfu Hui and Changzhou regiment commander and relief director Yao Feng, whom he sent to the emperor.

sentences.zh: （王钅至《默記》：李景聞世宗親至淮上，而滁州其控扼，且援壽州，命大將皇甫暉、監軍姚鳳提兵十萬扼其地。

translations.literal: (Wang Zhi's Silent Records: When Li Jing heard that Shizong had come in person to the Huai, and that Chuzhou was the strategic choke point and also relieved Shouzhou, he ordered the great generals Huangfu Hui and supervising general Yao Feng to lead one hundred thousand troops to hold that place.
translations.idiomatic: (From Wang Zhi's Silent Records: Learning that Shizong had reached the Huai in person, Li Jing knew Chuzhou controlled the route and could relieve Shouzhou; he sent Huangfu Hui and supervising general Yao Feng with one hundred thousand men to hold it.

sentences.zh: 太祖以周師數千與暉遇於清流關隘路，周師大敗，暉整全師入憩滁州城下，會翊日再出。

translations.literal: Taizu led several thousand Zhou troops and met Hui at the Qingliu Pass defile; the Zhou army suffered a great defeat. Hui reassembled his full force and encamped below Chuzhou, intending to come out again the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangyin led a few thousand Zhou troops against Hui at Qingliu Pass and was badly beaten. Hui rallied his whole force and rested below Chuzhou, planning to march out again the next day.

sentences.zh: 太祖兵聚關下，且虞暉兵再至，聞諸村人，雲有鎮州趙學究在村中教學，多智計，村民有爭訟者，多請以決曲直。

translations.literal: Taizu's troops gathered below the pass, fearing that Hui's army would return; he heard from the villagers that a certain Zhao Xuejiu of Zhenzhou was teaching in the village, very resourceful, and that villagers with disputes often asked him to decide right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangyin's troops massed at the pass, anxious that Hui would return. Villagers told him of Zhao Xuejiu from Zhenzhou, a village schoolmaster famed for his wits, whom locals often asked to settle disputes.

sentences.zh: 太祖往訪之，學究曰：「我有奇計，所謂因敗為勝，轉禍為福。

translations.literal: Taizu went to consult him; the scholar said: "I have a strange plan—what is called turning defeat into victory and misfortune into blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangyin sought him out. The scholar said, "I have a plan to turn defeat into victory and disaster into gain.

sentences.zh: 今關下有徑路，人無行者，雖牌軍亦不知之，乃山之背也，可以直抵城下。

translations.literal: Below the pass there is now a footpath that no one travels; even the guard cavalry do not know it—it lies on the reverse slope of the mountain and can reach the city directly.
translations.idiomatic: There is a path below the pass that no one uses—even the guard cavalry do not know it. It runs behind the mountain and leads straight to the walls.

sentences.zh: 方值西澗水大漲之時，彼必謂我既敗之後，無敢躡其後者，誠能由山背小路率兵浮西澗水至城下，斬關而入，可以得志。

translations.literal: Just when the Xijian River is in flood, they will surely think that after our defeat no one would dare follow them. If you can truly lead troops by the mountain path, ford the Xijian, reach the city, cut through the gate, and enter, you can achieve your aim.
translations.idiomatic: The Xijian is swollen now; they will assume that after our rout no one would dare follow. If you take the back path, swim the Xijian, and break in through the gate, you can still win.

sentences.zh: 」太祖大喜，且命學究以指其路，學究亦不辭，而遣人前導，即下令誓師，夜從小徑行，三軍跨馬浮西澗以迫城，暉果不為備。

translations.literal: " Taizu was greatly pleased and ordered the scholar to point out the way; the scholar did not refuse but sent men ahead as guides; he then ordered the army sworn and marched by the small path at night; the whole force crossed the Xijian on horseback to press the city; Hui indeed was unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangyin was delighted, had the scholar show the way, and accepted his guides. That night he rallied the troops, stole along the path, and led the whole army swimming the Xijian toward the walls. Hui, as expected, was caught off guard.

sentences.zh: 奪門以入，暉始聞之，率親兵擐甲與太祖巷戰，三縱而三擒之，遂下滁州。）〉

translations.literal: They seized the gate and entered; only then did Hui hear of it; he led his personal troops in armor to fight Taizu in the lanes; three times he was released and three times captured; thus Chuzhou was taken.)〉
translations.idiomatic: They stormed the gate. Hui, hearing too late, led his guards in armor into the alleys to fight Kuangyin; three times he broke free and three times was taken. Chuzhou fell.)〉

sentences.zh: 甲戌，江南國主李景遣泗州牙將王知朗賫書一函至滁州，本州以聞，書稱唐皇帝奉書於大周皇帝，其略云：「願陳兄事，永奉鄰歡，設或俯鑒遠圖，下交小國，悉班卒乘，俾乂蒼黔，慶雞犬之相聞，奉瓊瑤以為好，必當歲陳山澤之利，少助軍旅之須。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu the lord of Jiangnan Li Jing sent the Sizhou adjutant Wang Zhilang bearing a letter in one bundle to Chuzhou; the prefecture reported it. The letter styled itself as the Tang Emperor presenting a letter to the Great Zhou Emperor; in summary it said: "We wish to declare brotherly relations and forever keep neighborly goodwill. If you would deign to regard our distant design and condescend to treat our small state, dispatching troops in full array to bring peace to the black-haired masses, rejoicing that fowl and dog may hear one another across the border and offering jade and silk in friendship, we shall surely present each year the produce of mountains and marshes to assist somewhat the needs of your army."
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Li Jing of Jiangnan sent his Sizhou adjutant Wang Zhilang to Chuzhou with a letter addressed from the "Tang emperor" to the emperor of Great Zhou. The gist was a plea for brotherly ties and lasting peace: if the Zhou would accept their submission, deploy troops to pacify the realm, and allow neighborly intercourse, they would send yearly tribute from hill and marsh to help supply the campaign.

sentences.zh: 虔俟報章，以答高命，道塗朝坦，禮幣夕行」云。

translations.literal: We reverently await your reply to answer your lofty command; may the road be level by morning and gifts dispatched by evening," it said.
translations.idiomatic: We await your gracious reply; may the roads be clear by dawn and your envoys arrive with gifts by nightfall," it concluded.

sentences.zh: 書奏不答。

translations.literal: When the letter was memorialized, no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The court received the letter but gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，今上縶送所獲江南二將皇甫暉、姚鳳至行在，詔釋之。

translations.literal: On day yihai the heir apparent sent under guard to the imperial camp the two Jiangnan generals captured, Huangfu Hui and Yao Feng; an edict ordered their release.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the heir apparent sent the captured Jiangnan generals Huangfu Hui and Yao Feng to the imperial camp, where an edict ordered them freed.

sentences.zh: 壬午，江南國主李景遣其臣偽翰林學士戶部侍郎鐘謨、偽工部侍郎文理院學士李德明等奉表來上，敘願依大國稱臣納貢之意，仍進金器千兩，錦綺綾羅二千匹及禦衣、犀帶、茶茗、藥物等，又進犒軍牛五百頭，酒二千石。

translations.literal: On day renwu the lord of Jiangnan Li Jing sent his ministers the false Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Zhong Mo, the false Vice Minister of Works and Academician of the Wenli Academy Li Deming, and others to present a memorial stating their wish to submit to the great state as vassals and pay tribute; they also presented one thousand liang of gold vessels, two thousand bolts of brocade and gauze, imperial robes, rhinoceros belts, tea, medicines, and the like, and also presented five hundred oxen and two thousand shi of wine to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Li Jing sent Zhong Mo, his false Hanlin academician and vice minister of revenue, Li Deming, false vice minister of works and Wenli academician, and others with a memorial offering vassalage and tribute: a thousand liang of gold vessels, two thousand bolts of silks, imperial robes, rhinoceros-horn belts, tea, medicines, five hundred oxen, and two thousand shi of wine for the troops.

sentences.zh: 是日，賜謨等錦綺綾羅二百匹，銀器一百兩，襲衣、金帶、鞍馬等。

translations.literal: That day Mo and the others were given two hundred bolts of brocade and gauze, one hundred liang of silver vessels, robes, gold belts, saddled horses, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Zhong Mo's party received two hundred bolts of silk, a hundred liang of silverware, robes, gold belts, and horses.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，侍衛馬軍指揮韓令坤奏，收下揚州。

translations.literal: On day bingxu the Commander of the Imperial Horse Guards Han Lingkun memorialized that Yangzhou had been taken.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Han Lingkun, commander of the imperial horse guards, reported the capture of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·韓令坤傳》：率兵襲揚州，將吏開門以迎之，令坤整眾而入，市不易肆，人甚悅。）〉

translations.literal: (Eastern Capital Epitome, biography of Han Lingkun: He led troops in a surprise attack on Yangzhou; the officers opened the gates to welcome him; Lingkun entered with his forces in good order; the markets did not change their stalls; the people were greatly pleased.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Eastern Capital Epitome, biography of Han Lingkun: He stormed Yangzhou; the garrison opened the gates to welcome him. He entered in good order without disturbing the markets, to the people's great satisfaction.)〉

sentences.zh: 丁亥，壽州城內左神衛軍使徐象等一十八人來奔。

translations.literal: On day dinghai eighteen men including the Left Divine Guard commander Xu Xiang from within Shouzhou city came over to the Zhou side.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Xu Xiang, commander of the Left Divine Guard, and seventeen others defected from within Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，朗州節度使王進逵上言領兵入鄂州界，攻長山寨，殺賊軍三千餘眾。

translations.literal: On day gengyin the military governor of Langzhou Wang Jinkui reported leading troops into Ezhou territory, attacking Changshan Stockade and killing more than three thousand rebel troops.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Wang Jinkui of Langzhou reported entering Ezhou, storming Changshan Stockade, and killing over three thousand enemy troops.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，今上表偽命天長軍制置使耿謙以本軍降，獲糧草二千餘萬。

translations.literal: On day xinmao the heir apparent memorialized that the false appointee Commissioner of the Tianchang Army Geng Qian had surrendered with his entire force, and more than twenty million units of grain and fodder were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the heir apparent reported that Geng Qian, the enemy's commissioner of the Tianchang army, had surrendered with his whole force, yielding over twenty million units of grain and fodder.

sentences.zh: 侍衛馬軍都指揮使韓令坤上言，泰州降。

translations.literal: The Commander of the Imperial Horse Guards Han Lingkun reported that Taizhou had surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Han Lingkun, commander of the imperial horse guards, reported that Taizhou had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，荊南上言，朗州節度使王進逵為部將潘叔嗣所殺。

translations.literal: On day guisi Jingnan reported that the military governor of Langzhou Wang Jinkui had been killed by his subordinate officer Pan Shusi.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Jingnan reported that Wang Jinkui of Langzhou had been killed by his subordinate Pan Shusi.

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·王逵傳》：領眾逼宜春，道出長沙，耀兵金波亭，有蜜蜂集傘蓋中，占者以為不利，遂留長沙，令行營副使毛立領兵南下，以潘叔嗣、張文表為前鋒。

translations.literal: (Records of the Nine States, biography of Wang Kui: Leading his host to press Yichun, his route passed through Changsha; he displayed troops at Jinbo Pavilion; bees gathered on his parasol; diviners deemed this unlucky; he therefore remained at Changsha and ordered the deputy commander of the field headquarters Mao Li to lead troops south, with Pan Shusi and Zhang Wenbiao as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: (Records of the Nine States, biography of Wang Kui: Marching on Yichun he passed through Changsha and paraded at Jinbo Pavilion. When bees swarmed his parasol, diviners called it ill omen; he stayed in Changsha and sent deputy Mao Li south with Pan Shusi and Zhang Wenbiao in the van.

sentences.zh: 叔嗣怒，至澧陵擁眾而還。

translations.literal: Shusi was angry; reaching Liling he gathered troops and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Shusi turned back at Liling with his troops.

sentences.zh: 逵聞兵叛，乃乘輕舸奔歸武陵，叔嗣追殺之於朗州城外。）〉

translations.literal: Kui heard of the mutiny, boarded a light boat, and fled to Wuling; Shusi pursued and killed him outside Langzhou city.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the revolt, Kui fled by light boat to Wuling; Shusi overtook and killed him outside Langzhou.)〉

sentences.zh: 遣人詣潭州，請周行逢為帥，行逢至朗州，斬叔嗣於市。

translations.literal: Messengers were sent to Tanzhou to invite Zhou Xingfeng as commander; Xingfeng reached Langzhou and beheaded Shusi in the market.
translations.idiomatic: They sent to Tanzhou for Zhou Xingfeng as commander; when he arrived at Langzhou he executed Shusi in public.

sentences.zh: 三月丙申，行光州刺史何超奏，光州偽命都監張承翰以城歸順，尋授承翰集州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third month, on day bingshen, the acting prefect of Guangzhou He Chao memorialized that the false appointee Director Zhang Chenghan of Guangzhou had surrendered the city; Chenghan was soon appointed prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingshen, acting Guangzhou prefect He Chao reported that the enemy director Zhang Chenghan had surrendered the city; Chenghan was soon made prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 庚子，文武百僚再上表請聽樂，詔允之。

translations.literal: On day gengzi the civil and military officials again submitted a memorial requesting permission to hear music; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the civil and military officials again petitioned to resume music; the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 行舒州刺史郭令圖奏，收下舒州。

translations.literal: The acting prefect of Shuzhou Guo Lingtu memorialized that Shuzhou had been taken.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Shuzhou prefect Guo Lingtu reported the capture of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: （《隆平集·王審琦傳》：世宗征淮，舒州堅壁不下，以郭令圖為刺史，命審琦、司超將兵攻城，一夕拔之。

translations.literal: (Longping Collection, biography of Wang Shenqi: When Shizong campaigned on the Huai, Shuzhou held firm and would not yield; Guo Lingtu was made prefect; Shenqi and Si Chao were ordered to lead troops to storm the city and took it in one night.
translations.idiomatic: (Longping Collection, biography of Wang Shenqi: During the Huai campaign Shuzhou held out. Guo Lingtu was made prefect and Shenqi and Si Chao were sent to storm it; they took the city in a single night.

sentences.zh: 令圖入，復見逐於郡人。

translations.literal: When Lingtu entered, he was again driven out by the people of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingtu entered, the locals drove him out again.

sentences.zh: 審琦方進軍援黃州，聞令圖被逐，乃選騎銜枚襲城，夜敗其眾而復納之。）〉

translations.literal: Shenqi was advancing to relieve Huangzhou; hearing that Lingtu had been expelled, he selected cavalry with gags in their mouths to raid the city by night, defeated the crowd, and reinstalled him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi was marching to relieve Huangzhou; learning that Lingtu had been expelled, he sent cavalry on a silent night raid, routed the mob, and restored Lingtu to office.)〉

sentences.zh: 江南國主李景表送先隔過朝廷兵士一百五十人至行在。

translations.literal: The lord of Jiangnan Li Jing memorialized and sent to the imperial camp one hundred fifty soldiers of the court army previously cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing of Jiangnan returned one hundred fifty Zhou soldiers who had been cut off behind enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 其軍即蜀軍也，秦、鳳之役，為王師所擒，配隸諸軍，及渡淮，輒復南逸。

translations.literal: These troops were Shu soldiers; in the Qin-Feng campaign they had been captured by the imperial army and assigned to various units; when they crossed the Huai they repeatedly fled south again.
translations.idiomatic: They were Shu troops captured in the Qin-Feng campaign and distributed among Zhou units; whenever they crossed the Huai they fled south again.

sentences.zh: 帝怒其奔竄，盡戮之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry at their flight and had them all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, enraged at their desertion, had them all put to death.

sentences.zh: 丙午，江南國主李景遣其臣偽司空孫晟、偽禮部尚書王崇質等奉表來上，仍進金一千兩、銀十萬兩、羅綺二千匹，又進賞給將士茶絹金銀羅帛等。

translations.literal: On day bingwu the lord of Jiangnan Li Jing sent his ministers the false Minister of Works Sun Sheng, the false Minister of Rites Wang Chongzhi, and others to present a memorial, and also presented one thousand liang of gold, one hundred thousand liang of silver, and two thousand bolts of gauze and silk, and also presented tea, silk, gold, silver, and brocade to reward the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Li Jing sent his false minister of works Sun Sheng, false minister of rites Wang Chongzhi, and others with another memorial, plus a thousand liang of gold, a hundred thousand liang of silver, two thousand bolts of silk, and gifts of tea, silk, gold, and silver for the troops.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，兩浙奏，遣大將率兵攻常州。

translations.literal: On day gengxu the Two Zhes reported that they had sent a great general to lead troops to attack Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the Two Zhes reported dispatching a senior general to attack Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 延州留後李彥頵奏，蕃眾與部民為亂，尋與兵司都監閻綰掩殺，獲其酋帥高鬧兒等十人，磔於市。

translations.literal: The military governor of Yanzhou Li Yanbin memorialized that the tribal masses and local troops had rebelled; soon he and the Director of the Military Bureau Yan Guan made a surprise attack and killed them, capturing their chieftains including Gao Naor and ten others, who were dismembered in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanbin of Yanzhou reported a tribal and local uprising; with military bureau director Yan Guan he crushed it, captured ten chieftains including Gao Naor, and had them dismembered in public.

sentences.zh: 彥頵本賈人也，貪而好利，蕃漢之民怨其侵刻，故至於是。

translations.literal: Yanbin was originally a merchant, greedy and fond of profit; both tribal and Han subjects resented his exactions, and thus matters came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbin had been a merchant, greedy and grasping; tribal and Han subjects alike hated his exactions, which led to the revolt.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，賜江南李景書曰：

translations.literal: On day xinhai a letter was sent to Li Jing of Jiangnan, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the emperor sent Li Jing this letter:

sentences.zh: 頃自有唐失禦，天步方艱，巢、蔡喪亂之餘，朱、李戰爭之後，中夏多故，六紀於茲，海縣瓜分，英豪鼎峙，自為聲教，各擅烝黎，連衡而交結四夷，乘釁而憑陵上國。

translations.literal: Recently, since Tang lost the Mandate and the imperial path grew difficult, after the disorders of Huang Chao and Cai Jing, and after the wars of Zhu and Li, the Central Plain has known many troubles for six decades now; the counties of the realm were carved up, heroes stood like tripods, each setting up his own teachings and monopolizing the people, forming horizontal alliances and befriending the four barbarians, seizing openings to encroach on the central state.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tang lost the Mandate the throne has been imperiled. After Huang Chao and Cai Jing's ravages and the wars of Zhu Wen and Li Keyong, the heartland has suffered turmoil for sixty years. The realm was carved among rival lords, each proclaiming his own rule, courting barbarian allies, and pressing upon the central dynasty whenever chance allowed.

sentences.zh: 華風不競，否運所鐘，凡百有心，孰不興憤？

translations.literal: Chinese civilization could not compete; adverse fortune had struck its hour—who among all men of feeling did not rise in indignation?
translations.idiomatic: Chinese order faltered under heaven's ill favor; who among the loyal did not burn with indignation?

sentences.zh: 朕猥承先訓，恭荷永圖，德不迨於前王，道不方於往古。

translations.literal: I have humbly received my predecessors' instruction and reverently bear their long design; my virtue does not reach the former kings, my Way does not match the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: I have humbly inherited my forebears' charge and their long vision, yet my virtue falls short of former kings and my conduct cannot equal the sages of old.

sentences.zh: 然而擅一百州之富庶，握三十萬之甲兵，且農戰交修，士卒樂用，思欲報累朝之宿怨，刷萬姓之包羞。

translations.literal: Yet I hold the wealth of a hundred prefectures and command three hundred thousand armored troops; both farming and warfare are cultivated together, and the soldiers are glad to serve; I think to repay the accumulated wrongs of many reigns and wash away the shame wrapped around the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I command the wealth of a hundred prefectures and three hundred thousand armed men; agriculture and war are both in order and the troops are eager to fight. I mean to avenge the wrongs of many reigns and restore the people's honor.

sentences.zh: 是以踐位已來，懷安不暇，破幽、并之巨寇，收秦、鳳之全封，兵不告疲，民有餘力。

translations.literal: Therefore since I took the throne I have had no leisure for ease; I broke the great rebels of You and Bing, recovered the full territories of Qin and Feng; the army did not complain of weariness and the people still had surplus strength.
translations.idiomatic: Since my accession I have had no time for repose: I crushed the great foes of You and Bing and recovered Qin and Feng intact, without exhausting the army or the people.

sentences.zh: 一昨回軍隴上，問罪江幹，我實有辭，咎將誰執？

translations.literal: Just recently I turned the army on Longyou and called you to account on the Yangtze banks; I truly have right on my side—who shall bear the blame?
translations.idiomatic: Only lately I finished on the Longyou frontier and now bring the war to the Yangtze. The case is mine; who is to blame?

sentences.zh: 朕親提金鼓，尋渡淮、淝，上順天心，下符人欲，前鋒所向，彼眾無遺，棄甲僵屍，動盈川谷。

translations.literal: I personally took up drum and bell, soon crossed the Huai and Fei; above I accord with Heaven's mind, below I match men's desires; wherever the vanguard turned, none of their masses remained; cast-off armor and stiff corpses filled the valleys at every move.
translations.idiomatic: I took the field in person, crossed the Huai and Fei, and found heaven and men alike on my side. Where my van marched, the enemy left none alive; valleys choked with abandoned armor and the dead.

sentences.zh: 收城徇地，已過滁陽，豈有落其爪牙，折其羽翼，潰其心腹，扼其吭喉而不亡者哉！

translations.literal: Taking cities and sweeping territory, I have already passed Chuyang—how could there be one who loses his claws and fangs, breaks his wings, is routed in the vitals, and has his throat seized yet does not perish!
translations.idiomatic: City after city has fallen; I am already past Chuyang. When claws are broken, wings clipped, the heart routed, and the throat gripped, how can any state survive!

sentences.zh: 蚤者，泗州主將遞送到書一函；

translations.literal: Earlier the Sizhou commander forwarded a letter in one bundle;
translations.idiomatic: Some days ago your Sizhou commander forwarded a letter to us;

sentences.zh: 尋又使人鐘謨、李德明至，賫所上表及貢奉衣服腰帶、金銀器幣、茶藥牛酒等；

translations.literal: soon after your envoys Zhong Mo and Li Deming arrived, bearing the memorial you submitted and tribute of robes, belts, gold and silver vessels, tea, medicines, oxen, and wine;
translations.idiomatic: then Zhong Mo and Li Deming came with your memorial and gifts of robes, belts, gold and silver, tea, medicines, oxen, and wine;

sentences.zh: 今又使人孫晟等並到行朝。

translations.literal: now your envoys Sun Sheng and others have all reached the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: and now Sun Sheng and your other envoys have reached my camp.

sentences.zh: 觀其降身聽命，引咎告窮，所謂君子見機，不俟終日，茍非達識，孰能若斯？

translations.literal: Seeing you lower yourselves and heed commands, confess fault and declare exhaustion—this is what is called the gentleman perceiving the moment and not waiting till day's end; if not men of far sight, who could act thus?
translations.idiomatic: You bow to command, confess fault, and plead exhaustion—the wise man, seeing how matters stand, does not wait until evening; who but a man of true discernment could act thus?

sentences.zh: 但以奮武興戎，所以討不服；

translations.literal: Yet to rouse martial ardor and raise arms is the means to punish those who will not submit;
translations.idiomatic: Yet arms are raised to chastise the recalcitrant;

sentences.zh: 惇信明義，所以懷遠人。

translations.literal: to honor faith and clarify righteousness is the means to win over distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: and faith and righteousness are how distant peoples are won over.

sentences.zh: 五帝三王盛德大業，恒用此道，以正萬邦。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors and Three Kings in their great virtue and great undertakings constantly used this Way to set the myriad states aright.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors and Three Kings, in their great virtue and achievements, always used this principle to bring order to the realm.

sentences.zh: 朕今躬統戎師，龔行討伐，告於郊廟社稷，詢於將相公卿，天誘其衷，國無異論。

translations.literal: I now personally command the army of war, reverently carrying out punitive expedition, announcing it to the suburban altars, ancestral temples, and altars of soil and grain, consulting the generals, ministers, and chief ministers; Heaven guides my heart, and the state has no dissenting voices.
translations.idiomatic: I now lead the army in person on a righteous punitive campaign, having announced it to the spirits and consulted my generals and ministers. Heaven inclines my heart, and the court speaks with one voice.

sentences.zh: 茍不能恢復內地，申畫邊疆，便議班旋，真同戲劇，則何以光祖宗之烈，厭士庶之心，匪獨違天，兼且咈眾。

translations.literal: If I cannot recover the inner lands and redraw the frontier, yet discuss withdrawing the army, it would truly be like a play—how then could I glorify the ancestors' brilliance or satisfy the hearts of officers and commoners? This would not only defy Heaven but also go against the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: If I could not recover our lost heartland and secure the frontier yet talked of withdrawing the army, it would be mere theater—how could I honor our ancestors or satisfy soldiers and people alike? That would defy both Heaven and public will.

sentences.zh: 但以淮南部內，已定六州，盧、壽、濠、黃，大軍悉集，指期克日，拉朽焚枯，其餘數城，非足介意。

translations.literal: Yet within southern Huainan six prefectures are already secured—Lu, Shou, Hao, and Huang; the great army is all assembled; the day of capture is fixed; rotten wood will be pulled down and withered stalks burned; the remaining few cities are not worth concern.
translations.idiomatic: Within southern Huainan we have already secured six prefectures—Lu, Shou, Hao, and Huang. The main army is massed and victory is only a matter of days; what remains are a few cities hardly worth mention.

sentences.zh: 必若盡淮甸之土地，為大國之提封，猶是遠圖，豈同迷復。

translations.literal: If you must have all the lands of the Huai region as the great state's frontier, that is still a far-reaching design—how could it be the same as losing one's way and returning?
translations.idiomatic: To take all the Huai lands into the great state's borders is still a far-reaching aim—not the same as wandering lost and turning back.

sentences.zh: 如此則江南吏卒悉遣放還，江北軍民並當留住，免違物類之性，俾安鄉土之情。

translations.literal: If so, then all officials and soldiers of Jiangnan will be sent back, while military and civilians of Jiangbei will all be retained, avoiding violation of creatures' natures and allowing attachment to native soil and sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: In that case all Jiangnan officials and troops would be sent home, while Jiangbei soldiers and civilians would remain—respecting natural ties and letting each people rest in its own country.

sentences.zh: 至於削去尊稱，願輸臣禮，非無故事，實有前規。

translations.literal: As for stripping away exalted titles and wishing to offer ministerial rites, this is not without precedent; there truly are former regulations.
translations.idiomatic: As for surrendering your royal title and offering vassal obeisance, precedents exist and rules from former times apply.

sentences.zh: 蕭詧奉周，不失附庸之道；

translations.literal: Xiao Cha served Zhou without failing the way of a dependent state;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha served Zhou without failing the duties of a vassal;

sentences.zh: 孫權事魏，自同藩國之儀。

translations.literal: Sun Quan served Wei in the same ritual as a frontier state.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan treated with Wei on the footing of a tributary state.

sentences.zh: 古也雖然，今則不取，但存常號，何爽歲寒。

translations.literal: Ancient though such cases were, today I do not accept it; I will only preserve your ordinary title—what offense against the cold of year's end?
translations.idiomatic: Such were ancient precedents, but I will not take them today. I shall only let you keep your usual title—no breach of enduring obligation.

sentences.zh: 儻堅事大之心，終不迫人於險，事資真愨，辭匪枝遊，俟諸郡之悉來，即大軍之立罷。

translations.literal: If you firmly maintain a heart of serving the greater power, I will never drive men into peril; matters rely on true sincerity, words must not be branching evasions; when all commanderies have fully submitted, the great army will immediately be halted.
translations.idiomatic: If you remain steadfast in submission, I will not press you to the brink. Deal in good faith, not evasive words. When every district has surrendered, the main army will withdraw at once.

sentences.zh: 質於天地，信若丹青，我無彼欺，爾無我詐，言盡於此，更不煩雲，茍曰未然，請自茲絕。

translations.literal: Pledged before Heaven and Earth, faith like red and black ink—I will not deceive you, you will not cheat me; words end here and need no further clouds; if you say it is not so, let us break off from this moment.
translations.idiomatic: Before Heaven and Earth I pledge faith as binding as ink on silk: neither shall deceive the other. I have said all I mean to say. If you deny it, let relations end here.

sentences.zh: 竊以陽春在候，庶務縈思，願無廢於節宣，更自期於愛重。

translations.literal: I venture to think that spring is at hand and many affairs fill the mind; I hope you will not neglect moderation in conduct and will again set your heart on self-care.
translations.idiomatic: Spring is near and affairs press upon you; take care of your health and cherish yourself.

sentences.zh: 音塵非遠，風壤猶殊，翹想所深，勞於夢寐。

translations.literal: Our messages are not far apart, yet winds and soil still differ; what I long for deeply wearies me even in dreams.
translations.idiomatic: Though messages may pass between us, our lands remain apart. You are much in my thoughts, even in dreams.

sentences.zh: 又賜其將佐書曰：

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to their generals and assistants, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also sent this letter to their commanders:

sentences.zh: 朕自類祃出師，麾旄問罪，絕長淮而電擊，指建業以鷹揚，旦夕之間，克捷相繼。

translations.literal: Since I offered the war sacrifice and took the field, brandishing banners to call to account, crossing the long Huai in lightning strike and aiming at Jianye with hawk's soar, within days and nights victories followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Since I sacrificed and marched to war, striking across the Huai like lightning and bearing down on Jianye like a hawk, victories have followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 至若兵興之所自，釁起之所來，勝負之端倪，戎甲之次第，不勞盡諭，必想具知。

translations.literal: As for when the armies arose, when the quarrel began, the signs of victory and defeat, and the sequence of armored troops—there is no need to explain fully; you must already know in detail.
translations.idiomatic: How the war began, how the quarrel arose, and how battle has gone—you surely know without my recounting every detail.

sentences.zh: 近者金陵使人，繼來行闕，追悔前事，委質大朝，非無謝咎之辭，亦有罷軍之請，但以南邦之土地，本中夏之封疆，茍失克復之期，大辜朝野之望，已興是役，固不徒還，必若自淮以南，畫江為界，盡歸中國，猶是遠圖。

translations.literal: Recently envoys from Jinling have come in succession to the imperial camp, regretting past affairs and submitting to the great court; they have words of apology and also requests to halt the army—but the lands of the southern realm were originally the central state's territory; if the time of recovery is missed, court and countryside will be greatly disappointed; this campaign has been raised and will not return empty-handed; even if south of the Huai the Yangtze were taken as boundary and all returned to China, that would still be a far-reaching plan.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from Jinling have come repeatedly, repenting past conduct and submitting to the court, apologizing and asking us to halt the army. Yet the south was always central territory; to fail now would betray court and people alike. This campaign will not end without result. Even taking the Yangtze as border south of the Huai and restoring all to China would be only a modest aim.

sentences.zh: 所雲願為外臣，乞比湖、浙，彼既服義，朕豈忍人，必當別議封崇，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: What they say of wishing to be outer ministers and begging comparison with Hu and Zhe—since they have submitted to righteousness, how could I bear to press men? I shall certainly discuss separate enfeoffment and treat them with special rites.
translations.idiomatic: Their wish to become outer ministers like Hu and Zhe—now that they submit, how could I be harsh? I shall grant them honorable standing and special treatment.

sentences.zh: 凡爾將佐，各盡乃心，善為國家之謀，勉擇恒久之利。

translations.literal: All you generals and assistants, each give your full heart, plan well for the state, and strive to choose lasting advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Each of you commanders should give your whole heart to counsel what is best for your state and choose what will endure.

sentences.zh: 初，李景遣鐘謨、李德明奉表至行闕，使人面奏云：「本國主願割壽、濠、泗、楚、光、海六州之地，歸於大朝。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Jing sent Zhong Mo and Li Deming with a memorial to the imperial camp; the envoy reported in person: "Our lord wishes to cede the six prefectures of Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai to the great court."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Jing had sent Zhong Mo and Li Deming with a memorial; their envoy reported in person that their lord wished to cede Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai to the great court.

sentences.zh: 」帝志在盡取江北諸郡，不允其請。

translations.literal: " The Emperor's aim was to take all the commanderies north of the Yangtze; he did not grant the request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor aimed to recover every commandery north of the Yangtze and refused.

sentences.zh: 使人見王師急攻壽陽，李德明奏曰：「願陛下寬臣數日之誅，容臣自往江南，取本國表，盡獻江北之地。

translations.literal: The envoy saw the imperial army urgently attacking Shouyang; Li Deming memorialized: "I beg Your Majesty to grant me a few days' reprieve from punishment and allow me to go myself to Jiangnan to obtain our state's memorial and offer all the lands north of the Yangtze."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the imperial army pressing Shouyang, Li Deming pleaded: "Grant me a few days' grace to return to Jiangnan and bring back a memorial offering all lands north of the Yangtze."

sentences.zh: 」帝許之，乃令李德明、王崇質賫此書以賜李景。

translations.literal: " The Emperor granted it and ordered Li Deming and Wang Chongzhi to bear this letter as a gift to Li Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent Li Deming and Wang Chongzhi with these letters to Li Jing.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲子，以徐州節度使武行德為濠州城下行營都部署，以前鄧州節度使候章為壽州城下水寨都部署。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on day jiazi, the military governor of Xuzhou Wu Xingde was made overall commander of the camp below Haozhou city, and the former military governor of Dengzhou Hou Zhang was made commander of the water stockade below Shouzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on jiazi, Wu Xingde of Xuzhou was appointed commander below Haozhou, and former Dengzhou governor Hou Zhang commander of the water camp below Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 己巳，車駕發壽春，循淮而東。

translations.literal: On day jisi the imperial carriage departed Shouchun and followed the Huai eastward.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the emperor left Shouchun and marched east along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 辛未，揚州奏，江南大破兩浙軍於常州。

translations.literal: On day xinwei Yangzhou reported that Jiangnan had routed the Two Zhes' army at Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Yangzhou reported that Jiangnan had crushed the Two Zhes' forces at Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，兩浙錢俶承詔遣部將率兵攻常州，為江南大將陸孟俊所敗，將佐陷沒者甚眾，李景亦以表聞。

translations.literal: Earlier Qian Chu of the Two Zhes, obeying the edict, sent a subordinate general to attack Changzhou and was defeated by Jiangnan's great general Lu Mengjun; many officers were lost; Li Jing also reported this by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qian Chu of the Two Zhes had sent generals against Changzhou by imperial order but was beaten by Jiangnan's Lu Mengjun, losing many officers; Li Jing also reported the victory.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，駐蹕於濠州城下。

translations.literal: On day yihai he halted below Haozhou city.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai he encamped below Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，揚州韓令坤破江南賊軍於州之東境，獲大將陸孟俊。

translations.literal: On day dingchou Han Lingkun of Yangzhou defeated Jiangnan rebel troops on the eastern border of the prefecture and captured the great general Lu Mengjun.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Han Lingkun of Yangzhou routed Jiangnan forces east of the city and captured Lu Mengjun.

sentences.zh: 今上表大破江南軍於六合，斬首五千級。

translations.literal: The heir apparent memorialized a great defeat of Jiangnan troops at Liuhe, with five thousand heads taken.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent reported a great victory at Liuhe, taking five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 時李景乘常州之捷，遣陸孟俊領兵迫泰州，王師不守，韓令坤欲棄揚州而回。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jing, riding the victory at Changzhou, sent Lu Mengjun to lead troops against Taizhou; the imperial army did not hold firm; Han Lingkun wished to abandon Yangzhou and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by Changzhou, Li Jing sent Lu Mengjun against Taizhou. Zhou forces wavered and Han Lingkun considered abandoning Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，急遣殿前都指揮使張永德帥親兵往援之，又命今上領步騎二千人屯於六合。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and urgently sent the Commander of the Palace Front Zhang Yongde to lead personal troops to relieve them, and also ordered the heir apparent to lead two thousand infantry and cavalry to encamp at Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily sent Zhang Yongde of the palace guard with elite troops to reinforce them and ordered the heir apparent to camp at Liuhe with two thousand horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 俄而陸孟俊領其徒自海陵抵揚州，令坤迎擊，敗之，生擒孟俊。

translations.literal: Soon Lu Mengjun led his followers from Hailing to Yangzhou; Lingkun met and attacked him, defeated him, and captured Mengjun alive.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lu Mengjun marched from Hailing on Yangzhou; Lingkun met him, routed his force, and took Mengjun alive.

sentences.zh: 李景遣其弟齊王達率大眾由瓜步濟江，距六合一舍而設柵。

translations.literal: Li Jing sent his brother the Prince of Qi Li Da to lead a great host across the river from Guabu, encamping one li from Liuhe and setting palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing sent his brother Li Da, Prince of Qi, with a large army across from Guabu, pitching camp a li from Liuhe behind palisades.

sentences.zh: 居數日，乃棄柵來迫官軍。

translations.literal: After several days they abandoned the palisades and came to press the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: After several days they abandoned their camp and advanced on the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 今上麾兵以擊之，賊軍大敗，餘眾赴江溺死者不可勝紀。

translations.literal: The heir apparent commanded troops to strike them; the rebel army suffered a great defeat; the remainder rushed into the river and drowned beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent attacked; the enemy was routed and countless drowned fleeing into the river.

sentences.zh: 己卯，韓令坤奏，敗楚州賊將馬在貴萬餘眾於灣頭堰，獲漣州刺史秦進崇。

translations.literal: On day jimao Han Lingkun memorialized defeating more than ten thousand of Chuzhou rebel general Ma Zaigui's troops at Wantou Weir and capturing Lianzhou prefect Qin Jinchong.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Han Lingkun reported defeating over ten thousand troops under Chuzhou general Ma Zaigui at Wantou Weir and capturing Lianzhou prefect Qin Jinchong.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以宣徽南院使向訓為權淮南節度使，充沿江招討使；

translations.literal: On day bingxu the Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat Xiang Xun was made acting military governor of Huainan and commissioner for riverine pacification;
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Xiang Xun, commissioner of the southern bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made acting Huainan military governor and riverine pacification commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以侍衛馬軍都指揮使韓令坤充沿江副招討使。

translations.literal: the Commander of the Imperial Horse Guards Han Lingkun was made deputy riverine pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: with Han Lingkun, commander of the imperial horse guards, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·向拱傳》：揚州初平，南唐令境上出師謀收復，韓令坤有棄城之意，即驛召拱赴行在，拜淮南節度使，依前宣徽使兼沿江招討使，以令坤為副。

translations.literal: (Song History, biography of Xiang Gong: When Yangzhou was first pacified, Southern Tang ordered troops on the border to march and plan recovery; Han Lingkun had thoughts of abandoning the city; Gong was summoned by post horse to the imperial camp, appointed military governor of Huainan, retaining his former post as commissioner while also serving as riverine pacification commissioner, with Lingkun as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: (Song History, biography of Xiang Gong: After Yangzhou fell, Southern Tang tried to recover it; Han Lingkun thought of abandoning the city. Gong was summoned post-haste, made Huainan military governor, kept his palace post, and took riverine command with Lingkun as deputy.

sentences.zh: 時周師久駐淮陽，都將趙晁、白延遇等驕恣橫暴，不相稟從，惟務貪濫，至有劫人婦女者。

translations.literal: At that time the Zhou army had long encamped at Huaiyang; commanders Zhao Chao, Bai Yanyu, and others were arrogant and violent, did not obey orders, sought only greed and excess, and even seized other men's wives.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army had long camped at Huaiyang. Commanders Zhao Chao and Bai Yanyu grew arrogant, ignored orders, plundered freely, and even abducted women.

sentences.zh: 及拱至，戮其不法者數輩，軍中肅然。）〉

translations.literal: When Gong arrived he executed several lawless men, and the army became orderly.)〉
translations.idiomatic: When Gong arrived he executed several offenders and restored discipline.)〉

sentences.zh: 丁亥，車駕發濠州，幸渦口。

translations.literal: On day dinghai the imperial carriage departed Haozhou and visited Wokou.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the emperor left Haozhou for Wokou.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以前湖南節度使馬希崇為左羽林統軍。

translations.literal: On day jichou the former military governor of Hunan Ma Xichong was made commander of the Left Forest of Feathers Army.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou former Hunan governor Ma Xichong was made commander of the Left Forest of Feathers Army.

sentences.zh: 五月壬辰朔，以渦口為鎮淮軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day renchen, Wokou was made Zhenhuai Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the fifth month, Wokou was designated Zhenhuai Army.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，車駕還京，發渦口。

translations.literal: On day wuxu the imperial carriage returned to the capital, departing from Wokou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the emperor returned to the capital from Wokou.

sentences.zh: （馬令《南唐書》：天子駐於渦口，猶欲再幸揚州，宰相範質以師老泣諫，乃班師。）〉

translations.literal: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang: The Son of Heaven halted at Wokou and still wished to visit Yangzhou again; the chief minister Fan Zhi remonstrated with tears that the army was weary, and only then did they withdraw.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang: The emperor halted at Wokou and still meant to return to Yangzhou, but Fan Zhi wept that the army was exhausted, and the court withdrew.)〉

sentences.zh: 乙卯，上至自淮南，詔赦都下見禁罪人。

translations.literal: On day yimao the Emperor returned from Huainan; an edict pardoned prisoners under detention in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the emperor returned from Huainan and pardoned prisoners held in the capital.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，陳州節度使王令溫卒。

translations.literal: On day dingsi the military governor of Chenzhou Wang Lingwen died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Wang Lingwen, military governor of Chenzhou, died.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以江南偽命東都副留守、工部侍郎馮延魯為太府卿。

translations.literal: On day wuwu the false appointee Eastern Capital deputy military governor and Vice Minister of Works Feng Yanlu of Jiangnan was made Director of the Grand Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Feng Yanlu, the enemy's former Eastern Capital deputy governor and vice minister of works, was made Director of the Grand Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 己未，太子賓客於德辰卒。

translations.literal: On day jiwei the Guest of the Heir Apparent Yu Dechen died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Yu Dechen, guest of the heir apparent, died.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，詔：「天下公私織造布帛及諸色匹段，幅尺斤兩，並須依向來制度，不得輕弱假偽，犯者擒捉送官。

translations.literal: On day xinyou an edict: "Throughout the realm, whether public or private, woven cloth and silks and all kinds of bolt goods in width, length, and weight must follow the former regulations; they must not be light, weak, or falsely made; violators are to be seized and sent to the authorities."
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou an edict required all cloth and silk, public or private, to meet former standards of width and weight, forbidding shoddy or counterfeit goods on pain of arrest.

sentences.zh: 六月甲子，以鳳翔節度使王景為秦州節度使，兼西面沿邊都部署；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on day jiazi, the military governor of Fengxiang Wang Jing was made military governor of Qinzhou and also overall commander of the western frontier;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiazi, Wang Jing of Fengxiang was made Qinzhou governor and overall western frontier commander;

sentences.zh: 以宣徽南院使、陳州節度使向訓為淮南節度使，依前南院宣徽使，加檢校太尉；

translations.literal: the Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and military governor of Chenzhou Xiang Xun was made military governor of Huainan, retaining his former southern bureau post, with the added title of Grand Guardian;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun, southern bureau commissioner and Chenzhou governor, was confirmed Huainan military governor with the added title Grand Guardian;

sentences.zh: 以曹州節度使韓通為許州節度使，加檢校太尉；

translations.literal: the military governor of Caozhou Han Tong was made military governor of Xuzhou, with the added title of Grand Guardian;
translations.idiomatic: Han Tong of Caozhou was transferred to Xuzhou as Grand Guardian;

sentences.zh: 以亳州防禦使王全斌為隴州防禦使，遙領利州昭武軍兩使留後。

translations.literal: the defense commissioner of Bozhou Wang Quanbin was made defense commissioner of Longzhou, remotely holding the two-commissioner regency of Lizhou Zhaowu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quanbin of Bozhou was made Longzhou defense commissioner and held the Lizhou Zhaowu regency in absentia.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，許州王彥超移鎮永興軍，鄧州田景鹹移鎮鄜州。

translations.literal: On day bingyin Wang Yanchao of Xuzhou was transferred to Yongxing Army; Tian Jingxian of Dengzhou was transferred to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Wang Yanchao moved from Xuzhou to Yongxing Army and Tian Jingxian from Dengzhou to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞楊昭儉、知雜侍御史趙礪、侍御史張糾並停任，坐鞫獄失實也。

translations.literal: The Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Zhaojian, the miscellaneous investigating attendant censor Zhao Li, and the attendant censor Zhang Jiu were all suspended for errors in trying cases.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Yang Zhaojian, investigating censor Zhao Li, and attendant censor Zhang Jiu were dismissed for mishandling trials.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以翰林學士、戶部侍郎陶穀為兵部侍郎，充翰林學士承旨；

translations.literal: On day dingmao the Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Tao Gu was made Vice Minister of War and Chief Hanlin Academician;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Tao Gu, Hanlin academician and vice minister of revenue, became vice minister of war and chief Hanlin academician;

sentences.zh: 以水部員外郎知制誥扈載、度支員外郎王著，並本官充翰林學士；

translations.literal: the Water Bureau vice director and drafter of edicts Hu Zai and the Revenue Bureau vice director Wang Zhu were both made Hanlin Academicians in their present ranks;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zai of the Water Bureau and Wang Zhu of the Revenue Bureau were made Hanlin academicians;

sentences.zh: 以給事中高防為右散騎常侍；

translations.literal: the Supervising Secretary Gao Fang was made Right Regular Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Gao Fang became Right Regular Attendant;

sentences.zh: 以前都官郎中、知制誥薛居正為左諫議大夫，充昭文館學士，判館事。

translations.literal: the former Director of the Bureau of Review Xue Juzheng, drafter of edicts, was made Left Remonstrance Counselor, Academician of the Zhaowen Hall, and administrator of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: former review bureau director Xue Juzheng became Left Remonstrance Counselor, Zhaowen Hall academician, and hall administrator.

sentences.zh: 壬申，曲赦淮南道諸州見禁罪人，自今年六月十一日已前，凡有違犯，無問輕重，並不窮問。

translations.literal: On day renshen a partial amnesty was granted to prisoners under detention in the Huainan circuit prefectures; for offenses before the eleventh day of the sixth month of this year, whether light or heavy, no further inquiry would be made.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen a partial amnesty freed prisoners in Huainan for offenses before the eleventh of the sixth month, without further inquiry regardless of severity.

sentences.zh: 先屬江南之時，應有非理科徭，無名配率，一切停罷雲。

translations.literal: During the time when they belonged to Jiangnan, there had been unreasonable corvée and nameless levies—all were halted.
translations.idiomatic: All irregular corvée and unauthorized levies imposed under Jiangnan rule were abolished.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以右衛上將軍扈彥珂為太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: On day wuyin the Right Guard senior general Hu Yanke was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Hu Yanke, senior general of the Right Guard, retired as grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以西京留守王晏為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: On day gengchen the Western Capital military governor Wang Yan was made military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Western Capital governor Wang Yan was made Fengxiang military governor.

sentences.zh: 戊子，升贍國軍為濱州。

translations.literal: On day wuzi the Shanguo Army was promoted to Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Shanguo Army was elevated to Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮南道招討使李重進奏，壽州賊軍攻南寨，王師不利。

translations.literal: The Huainan pacification commissioner Li Chongjin memorialized that Shouzhou rebel troops had attacked the southern stockade and the imperial army had fared badly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin, Huainan pacification commissioner, reported that Shouzhou rebels had stormed the southern camp and beaten imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔步軍都指揮使李繼勛營於壽州之南，攻賊壘。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had ordered the Commander of the Foot Soldiers Li Jixun to encamp south of Shouzhou and attack rebel fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Jixun, commander of the foot army, had been ordered to camp south of Shouzhou and assault enemy works.

sentences.zh: 是日，賊軍出城來攻我軍，破柵而入，其攻城之具並為賊所焚，將士死者數百人。

translations.literal: That day rebel troops came out of the city to attack our army, broke through the palisade and entered; their siege equipment was all burned by the rebels, and several hundred officers and soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: That day the rebels sallied out, broke the palisade, burned the siege equipment, and killed several hundred Zhou troops.

sentences.zh: 李重進在東寨，亦不能救。

translations.literal: Li Chongjin was in the eastern stockade and could not rescue them either.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin in the eastern camp could not relieve them.

sentences.zh: 時城堅未下，師老於外，加之暑毒，糧運不繼。

translations.literal: At that time the walls were strong and the city had not fallen; the army was weary abroad; moreover there was poisonous summer heat and grain transport did not continue.
translations.idiomatic: The city still held, the army was worn down in the field, summer heat was fierce, and supplies ran short.

sentences.zh: 李繼勛喪失之後，軍無固誌，諸將議欲退軍，賴今上自六合領兵歸闕，過其城下，因為駐留旬日，王師復振。

translations.literal: After Li Jixun's defeat the army had no firm will; the generals discussed withdrawing; thanks to the heir apparent leading troops back to the capital from Liuhe and passing below the city, he therefore halted for ten days, and the imperial army revived.
translations.idiomatic: After Jixun's defeat morale collapsed and officers talked of retreat. The heir apparent, returning from Liuhe to the capital, paused ten days below the walls and restored the army's spirit.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛卯朔，以武清軍節度使、知潭州軍府事周行逢為朗州大都督，充武平軍節度使，加檢校太尉、兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the first day xinmao, the military governor of Wuqing Army and administrator of Tanzhou military affairs Zhou Xingfeng was made Grand Governor of Langzhou and military governor of Wuping Army, with the added titles of Grand Guardian and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On the autumn new moon of the seventh month, Zhou Xingfeng of Wuqing and Tanzhou was made grand governor of Langzhou and Wuping military governor, with the added titles Grand Guardian and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以太子賓客盧價為禮部尚書致仕，以給事中李明為大理卿。

translations.literal: On day dingyou the Guest of the Heir Apparent Lu Jia was made Minister of Rites and retired; the Supervising Secretary Li Ming was made Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Lu Jia, guest of the heir apparent, retired as minister of rites, and Supervising Secretary Li Ming became director of judicial review.

sentences.zh: 庚子，盧州行營都部署劉重進奏，破淮賊千餘於州界。

translations.literal: On day gengzi the overall commander of the Luzhou field camp Liu Chongjin memorialized defeating more than a thousand Huainan rebels on the prefectural border.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Liu Chongjin, commander of the Luzhou field camp, reported routing over a thousand rebels on the border.

sentences.zh: 丁未，濠州行營都部署武行德奏，敗淮賊二千人於州界。

translations.literal: On day dingwei the overall commander of the Haozhou field camp Wu Xingde memorialized defeating two thousand Huainan rebels on the prefectural border.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Wu Xingde of Haozhou reported defeating two thousand rebels on the border.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，太子太保王仁裕卒。

translations.literal: On day gengxu the Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Wang Renyu died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Wang Renyu, grand preceptor of the heir apparent, died.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，皇后符氏薨。

translations.literal: On day xinhai the Empress née Fu died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Empress Fu died.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使向訓自揚州班師，回駐壽春。

translations.literal: The military governor of Huainan Xiang Xun withdrew his army from Yangzhou and returned to encamp at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xun, Huainan military governor, withdrew from Yangzhou and encamped again at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 時王師攻壽春，經年未下，江、淮盜賊充斥，舒、蘄、和、泰等州復為吳人所據，故棄揚州並力於壽春焉。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial army attacked Shouchun for a year without taking it; bandits filled the Yangtze and Huai regions; Shu, Qi, He, and Tai prefectures were again held by Wu men; therefore Yangzhou was abandoned to concentrate force on Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Shouchun had dragged on a year while bandits roamed the Jiang-Huai region and Shu, Qi, He, and Tai fell back to Wu control, so Yangzhou was abandoned to concentrate on Shouchun.

sentences.zh: （馬令《南唐書》：向訓請棄揚州，並力以攻壽春，乃封府庫付主者，遣淮南舊將按巡城中，秋毫不犯而去。

translations.literal: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang: Xiang Xun requested abandoning Yangzhou to concentrate force on attacking Shouchun; he then sealed the treasury and entrusted it to custodians, sent former Huainan generals to patrol the city, and departed without violating so much as an autumn hair.
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang: Xiang Xun asked to abandon Yangzhou and focus on Shouchun. He sealed the treasury, left it in trustworthy hands, sent former Huainan officers to patrol the city, and withdrew without harming the people.

sentences.zh: 淮人大悅，皆負糗糧以送周師。）〉

translations.literal: The Huai people were greatly pleased and all carried dry rations to send off the Zhou army.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The people rejoiced and brought provisions to see the Zhou army off.)〉

sentences.zh: 八月壬戌，河陽白重贊移鎮涇州，張澤移鎮河中。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day renxu, Bai Chongzan of Heyang was transferred to Jingzhou, and Zhang Ze was transferred to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renxu, Bai Chongzan moved from Heyang to Jingzhou and Zhang Ze to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以前鄧州節度使侯章復為鄧州節度使，以侍衛步軍都指揮使、彰信軍節度使李繼勛為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: On day jiazi the former military governor of Dengzhou Hou Zhang was again made military governor of Dengzhou; the Commander of the Imperial Foot Soldiers and military governor of Zhangxin Army Li Jixun was made military governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi former Dengzhou governor Hou Zhang returned to Dengzhou, and Li Jixun, commander of the foot army and Zhangxin governor, was made Heyang military governor.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，太僕卿劇可久停任，坐為舉官累也。

translations.literal: On day yichou the Director of the Imperial Stud Ju Kejiu was suspended for being implicated as a recommending official.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Ju Kejiu, director of the imperial stud, was dismissed for a fault in recommending an official.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，端明殿學士王樸撰成新歷上之，命曰《顯德欽天曆》，上親為制序，仍付司天監行用。

translations.literal: On day wuchen the Academician of the Duanming Hall Wang Pu completed a new calendar and presented it; it was named the Xiande Imperial Heaven Calendar; the Emperor personally composed the preface and ordered the Directorate of Astronomy to put it into use.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Wang Pu of the Duanming Hall presented the new Xiande Imperial Heaven Calendar, for which the emperor wrote the preface and ordered the Directorate of Astronomy to adopt it.

sentences.zh: 殿前都指揮使張永德奏，破淮賊於下蔡。

translations.literal: The Commander of the Palace Front Zhang Yongde memorialized defeating Huainan rebels at Xiaocai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde, commander of the palace front, reported defeating Huainan rebels at Xiaocai.

sentences.zh: 先是，江南李景以王師猶在壽州，遣其將林仁肇、郭廷謂率水陸軍至下蔡，欲奪浮梁，以舟實薪芻，乘風縱火，永德禦之。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Jing of Jiangnan, because the imperial army was still at Shouzhou, sent his generals Lin Renzhao and Guo Tingyu to lead land and water forces to Xiaocai, wishing to seize the pontoon bridge; they loaded boats with fuel and fodder and set fire with the wind; Yongde defended against them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Jing, while the Zhou army remained at Shouzhou, sent Lin Renzhao and Guo Tingyu with land and river forces to Xiaocai to seize the pontoon bridge, loading boats with fuel to burn it downwind. Yongde met them.

sentences.zh: 有頃，風勢倒指，賊眾稍卻，因為官軍所敗。

translations.literal: Before long the wind shifted direction; the rebel masses retreated somewhat and were therefore defeated by the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the wind turned, the enemy fell back, and the imperial army routed them.

sentences.zh: 己卯，工部侍郎王敏停任，坐薦子婿陳南金為河陽記室也。

translations.literal: On day jimao the Vice Minister of Works Wang Min was suspended for recommending his son-in-law Chen Nanjin as secretary of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Wang Min, vice minister of works, was dismissed for appointing his son-in-law Chen Nanjin secretary at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 九月丙午，以端明殿學士、左散騎常侍、權知開封府事王樸為尚書戶部侍郎，充樞密副使；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on day bingwu, the Academician of the Duanming Hall, Left Regular Attendant, and acting administrator of Kaifeng prefecture Wang Pu was made Vice Minister of Revenue in the Secretariat and Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingwu, Wang Pu of the Duanming Hall, Left Regular Attendant, and acting Kaifeng administrator became vice minister of revenue and deputy commissioner of military affairs;

sentences.zh: 以右羽林統軍焦繼勛為左屯衛上將軍；

translations.literal: the Commander of the Right Forest of Feathers Army Jiao Jixun was made senior general of the Left Encampment Guard;
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Jixun of the Right Forest of Feathers Army became senior general of the Left Encampment Guard;

sentences.zh: 以左衛上將軍楊承信為右羽林統軍；

translations.literal: the senior general of the Left Guard Army Yang Chengxin was made Commander of the Right Forest of Feathers Army;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chengxin of the Left Guard became commander of the Right Forest of Feathers Army;

sentences.zh: 以左監門上將軍宋延渥為右神武統軍。

translations.literal: the senior general of the Left Gate Army Song Yanwo was made Commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yanwo of the Left Gate Army became commander of the Right Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛酉，葬宣懿皇后於懿陵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on day xinyou, the Xuanyi Empress was buried at Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on xinyou, Empress Xuanyi was buried at Yiling.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以右神武統軍宋延渥為廬州行營副部署。

translations.literal: On day guihai the Commander of the Right Divine Martial Army Song Yanwo was made deputy overall commander of the Luzhou field camp.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Song Yanwo, commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, was made deputy commander of the Luzhou field camp.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，舒州刺史郭令圖責授虢州教練使，坐棄郡逃歸也。

translations.literal: On day yichou the prefect of Shuzhou Guo Lingtu was demoted and appointed drill instructor of Guozhou for abandoning his commandery and fleeing back.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Shuzhou prefect Guo Lingtu was demoted to drill instructor at Guozhou for abandoning his post and fleeing home.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，詔曰：「諸司職員皆系奏補，當執役之際，悉藉公勤，及聽選之時，尤資幹敏，茍非慎擇，漸致因循。

translations.literal: On day bingyin an edict said: "Staff of all offices are appointed by memorial; when performing duties they all rely on public diligence, and at the time of selection especially need capability and alertness; if not carefully chosen, slackness will gradually arise."
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin an edict declared that all office staff were appointed by memorial and must serve diligently; without careful selection, slackness would spread.

sentences.zh: 應諸司寺監，今後收補役人，並須人材俊利，身言可采，書劄堪中，自前行止，委無訛濫，勒本司關送吏部，引驗人材，考校筆劄。

translations.literal: All directorates and supervisory offices, when hereafter recruiting service personnel, must all have sharp talent, acceptable bearing and speech, and writing that passes standard; their past conduct must truly be without fraud; their office is ordered to send them to the Ministry of Personnel with credentials; their talent is verified and their writing examined.
translations.idiomatic: All ministries and directorates recruiting clerks must choose able men of good bearing and competent writing, verify their records, and send them to the Ministry of Personnel for examination.

sentences.zh: 其中選者，連所試書跡及正身引過中書，余從前後格敕處分，仍每年只得一度奏補。

translations.literal: Those selected among them, together with their trial handwriting and in person, are led past the Secretariat; the rest follow former regulations and edicts; still, each year only one memorial appointment is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed were presented with their writing samples to the Secretariat; others followed existing rules, and each office might submit appointments only once a year.

sentences.zh: 」丁卯，宣懿皇后神主入廟，時有司請為後立別廟，禮也。

translations.literal: " On day dingmao the spirit tablet of the Xuanyi Empress entered the temple; at that time the relevant offices requested establishing a separate temple for the empress—this was ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the spirit tablet of Empress Xuanyi entered the ancestral temple; the ritual offices asked to establish a separate temple for her, as custom required.

sentences.zh: 己巳，詔：「漳河以北郡縣，並許鹽貨通商，逐處有鹼鹵之地，一任人戶煎煉。

translations.literal: On day jisi an edict: "North of the Zhang River, all commanderies and counties are permitted salt goods for trade; wherever there is alkaline brine land, households are entirely free to boil and refine."
translations.idiomatic: On jisi an edict allowed salt trade north of the Zhang River and permitted households to boil brine wherever alkaline deposits were found.

sentences.zh: 」壬申，以武平軍節度副使、知潭州軍府事宇文瓊為武清軍節度使，知潭州軍府事。

translations.literal: " On day renshen the deputy military governor of Wuping Army and administrator of Tanzhou military affairs Yuwen Qiong was made military governor of Wuqing Army and administrator of Tanzhou military affairs.
